findings.statement: Modified REQ-RL-001 rejects 2^53+1 for W and source values, but existing tests carrying SCN-RL-004 and SCN-RL-006 tokens assert the old reading: tests/test_rate_limiter.py test_scn_rl_004_window_in_float_range_accepted (W=2**53+1 accepted) and test_scn_rl_006_clock_value_float_reading (source 2**53+1 and 2**53+11 accepted with rounding). tasks.md 1.2 says SCN-RL-004/SCN-RL-006 tests 'still pass' and no task rewrites them, so after task 1.1 they fail; SCN-RL-004/006 test evidence would contradict the spec.
findings.recommendation: Add a task: remove 2**53+1 from the SCN-RL-004 accepted-W test and rewrite the SCN-RL-006 source-value test (2**53+1, 2**53+11 now ValueError) or move these cases under SCN-RL-007; fix the check of task 1.2 accordingly.

findings.statement: 'Value of type int or float (not bool)' does not say whether subclasses count. design.md Risks declares an int subclass with overridden __eq__ 'out of contract, as before', but no spec text says so; with D-1 a float subclass overriding __eq__ (reflected first) or an int subclass overriding __float__ can make an exactly representable value fail seconds == value, contradicting 'float - any finite value'. The new equality check makes the result depend on these methods.
findings.recommendation: State in REQ-RL-001 that subclasses of int/float with overridden numeric or comparison methods are outside the contract, or define the rule on the numeric value (e.g. int(value)/float(value) of the base type).

findings.statement: Main spec cites UNK-RL-001 (Change rate-limiter decision), and this Change's record also holds UNK-RL-001 with a different text (number reservation). After archive the id resolves to two records; the spec reference assumes UNK ids are unique across Changes. proposal.md documents this.
findings.recommendation: Optionally qualify the reference (e.g. rate-limiter/UNK-RL-001) or leave as is; the reservation is explained.

proposals.change: Task to update SCN-RL-004/SCN-RL-006 tests that assert 2**53+1 acceptance; task 1.2 check aligned (F-1).
REQ-RL-001: int/float subclasses with overridden __eq__/__float__ outside the contract (F-2).

assumptions.statement: Python semantics inferred without running code: float == int compares exactly; float(int subclass) calls overridden __float__; a float subclass overriding __eq__ gets the reflected call first.
Findings F-2..F-8 of review RUN-01M3FVYX2AN1AYX48W047KT7BA are non-goals and not repeated; the unchanged parts of REQ-RL-001 match main spec verbatim.
